# 123go.taxi

> Turns an address into a QR code a taxi driver scans to start navigation in their own app (Google Maps, Yandex, Waze, Apple Maps, any other). Free, open source, no accounts, nothing collected.

Businesses (restaurants, hotels, venues) can put a "Get here by taxi" button and QR on their website. Full instructions, written to be followed exactly by an AI assistant: https://github.com/Charles0xhorizonxyz/123gotaxi/blob/main/docs/ADD-TO-YOUR-WEBSITE.md

## Link format

https://123go.taxi/#v=1&lat=<LAT>&lon=<LON>&n=<NAME>&a=<ADDRESS>

- lat, lon: decimal degrees of the entrance, max 5 decimals. Required.
- n: public name of the place, max 60 characters, URL-encoded (spaces as +). Recommended.
- a: readable street address, max 100 characters, URL-encoded. Optional.
- via: earlier stops, "lat,lon~lat,lon", max 3. Optional.
- Everything stays after "#" (never sent to a server). Add no other parameters and never shorten the link.

Example: https://123go.taxi/#v=1&lat=41.02564&lon=28.97417&n=Galata+Kulesi&a=Bereketzade,+Beyo%C4%9Flu

## QR code

Encode exactly that link, error correction level Q, margin 2+, black on white, PNG 360 px or larger. 123go.taxi doesn't serve QR images: generate your own.
